post.description:
Some Submissions may require supporting documents to be uploaded. To find these use the following

GET /submissions?template=false&statuses=orange,red

This will return a list of submissions that have been orange or red routed. Each submission will state whether it requires a file to be uploaded via the submission.documents_upload_requested property. If this is true you can upload supporting documents. 

To know which documents to upload you can view the submission.latest_state.message property. This will provide a textual description of each of the documents required to be uploaded. Please note, check submission.latest_state.documents_upload_requested is true to ensure the latest state is referring to a document upload before displaying the text.

tags.name: Overview
tags.description:
This document will provide a brief overview of how to interface with the Customs Window Api.

The Api is REST based and utilises standard HTTP verbs (GET, POST, DELETE etc…) to expose various functionality across the Platform. This document will highlight the main use cases of integrating with the Customs Window Api. To call the Api use the following url:

 Production Base URL: https://api.customswindow.com

Development Base URL: https://api-dev.customswindow.com

tags.name: Authentication
tags.description:
The Customs Window API uses Secret keys to authenticate requests. A Secret Key is tied to the user who generates it. Meaning a key has the same permissions as the user who generates it. This allows you to have very granular permissions while also attributing actions to specific users.

As Secret Keys carry many permissions to your data, you must ensure they are kept secure. Do not store them on your VCS, client-side code etc… Secret Keys should remain secret and never be publicly available. If your Secret Key has been compromised or you would like to rotate it please use the dashboard to do so.

Authentication to the API is performed via HTTP Basic Auth.  Provide your Secret Key as the basic auth username value. You do not need to provide a password. All API requests should be made over HTTPS. Calls made over plain HTTP will be redirected to HTTPs. Restricted API requests without authentication will also fail.

tags.name: Pagination
tags.description:
In order to serve requests efficiently API endpoints that return lists will paginate their responses. I.e. an endpoint that can return a list of 100 objects will instead return the first 20 objects with a “next” param to access the next 20 objects and so forth. 

You can specify the amount of objects to be returned by using the page_size=XX parameter. The value provided here must be in the range of 5 to 40 or will be ignored and default to 20.

By default list endpoints use cursor based pagination. If instead you would like to use page based pagination you can pass the pagination_type=page parameter. Using page based pagination will also return the ‘count’ of objects (e.g. 100 in this case) to allow you to know the number of pages. Please note however page based pagination can return duplicates across pages if new data is inputted.

tags.name: Archived / Deleted Objects
tags.description: Various endpoints across the Api will allow you to DELETE objects. The DELETE operation in most cases performs a soft delete. As such DELETED objects are generally retrievable by passing the objects=deleted/all query parameter
